leg: LANE 1 — All Saints in Poland (Dubrovnik Oct 25 → Kraków/Warsaw → SFO by Nov 2), family of 5, fully costed both directions with points alternative
summary:
THE ANSWER TO YOUR TIMING PROBLEM IS THAT IT ISN'T ONE — AND IT'S FREE TO SOLVE.

Kraków sunset Nov 1 is 16:19, and I found the two candidate exits are literally the same airplane. SAS departs KRK 20:30 on Nov 1, sits 14h30 in Copenhagen, and lands SFO Nov 2 at 14:50 — $3,707/5. SAS departs KRK 10:15 on Nov 2, connects 45 min in Copenhagen, and lands SFO Nov 2 at 14:50 — $3,362/5. Same arrival, same CPH-SFO flight. Flying the NEXT day is $345 CHEAPER, replaces an overnight in an airport with a night in your own Kraków apartment, and cuts the journey from 27h20 to 13h35. You stay for the full Nov 1 evening and you are not punished for it. Nov 2 is the single cheapest Poland exit I pulled across six city-dates.

WHICH CITY IS ACTUALLY BETTER — KRAKÓW, decisively, and it isn't close for a family. (1) Rakowicki is ~1.5 km from the Old Town, one tram to the end of the line; Warsaw's Powązki is ~4 km out in a sprawling capital. (2) Kraków gives you a genuine two-act evening: Rakowicki for scale and sepulchral art, then Salwator — a hillside cemetery under Kościuszko Mound with a valley view over the city and a crypt that opens to visitors on Nov 1. Warsaw has no equivalent viewpoint. (3) Kraków's Old Town is intact medieval, which reads as "old Europe" to a 16/13/8-year-old; Warsaw's was rebuilt after 1945. (4) Kraków runs extra late tram lines, candle-and-flower stalls at the gates, and a 7pm concert at Rakowicki. (5) The daytime anchors are better: Wieliczka Salt Mine is a genuine kid hit. HONEST COUNTERPOINT: In Your Pocket says Rakowicki "can feel like a bit of a circus on 1 November" — it is crowded, and New Podgórze is the quiet alternative if that matters to you.

ON OCT 31 vs NOV 1 — you don't have to choose. Znicze (Polish grave candles) burn for up to a week, and photographic accounts specifically describe candle-glow matching the sunset at Salwator on the evening BEFORE All Saints. Arrive Oct 26 and you get the build-up, All Saints' Eve on the 31st, AND the Nov 1 peak. Nov 2 (Zaduszki) is not a public holiday, so shops and restaurants reopen — useful, because Nov 1 IS a bank holiday and most museums close.

THE "CHEAP SHORT VERSION" IS A MIRAGE. Ryanair DBV→KRK only flies Mon+Sat: Oct 26 (15:15) or Oct 31 (09:15). Taking Oct 31 leaves a SIX-NIGHT hole from your Oct 25 Dubrovnik checkout, and Dubrovnik costs more per night than Kraków does. Filling that gap in Croatia makes the "2-night" trip $6,740 all-in versus $6,527 for the full 7 nights in Poland — you pay $213 MORE for five fewer days. It only makes sense if another lane is already paying for Oct 25-31, in which case the marginal Kraków add-on is $4,400. Note also that even the Oct 26 flight forces one extra Dubrovnik night on Oct 25; I've costed that into every option's inbound.

AIRFARE, BOTH DIRECTIONS, TRUE 5-PASSENGER PRICING, PULLED LIVE TODAY. IN: Ryanair FR5916 DBV 15:15 → KRK 16:55 Oct 26, $191 for all five, verified off Ryanair's own API — still the only carrier selling 5 seats out of Dubrovnik. OUT: KRK→SFO Nov 1 $3,509 (n=16), Nov 2 $3,362 (n=18), Nov 3 $4,889 (n=1, avoid). WAW→SFO Nov 1 $3,550 (n=9), Nov 2 $4,538 (n=6), Nov 3 $3,550 (n=3). Your earlier $3,379 KRK / $3,028 WAW anchors did not reproduce today — Kraków came in $130 higher and Warsaw $522 higher, so treat those two numbers as stale. I also checked Sacramento: KRK→SMF $5,357 and WAW→SMF $3,872, both materially worse than SFO. Fly into SFO.

THE POINTS ALTERNATIVE. Flying Blue KRK→AMS→SFO at the 25,000-mile economy saver, with the Kraków feeder free under origin-destination pricing: 125,000 Amex MR for all five, plus roughly $875 in fees. That drops the trip from $6,527 to about $4,040 — 125,000 miles buying $2,487 of airfare, i.e. 1.99 cents per mile, out of the 525,000 MR you hold. The 2-business + 3-economy split is 195,000 miles plus about $1,425 in fees. TWO HONEST WARNINGS: the $175/person fee figure is an ESTIMATE, not a quote — Flying Blue raised economy surcharges about $60 in 2026 and Europe-to-US is the expensive direction; only flyingblue.com at checkout gives you the real euro number. And I could NOT verify saver space — that requires a logged-in search. Book the party as 2 and 3 on separate awards, because Flying Blue reprices the whole party up if one saver bucket can't hold everyone. On Kraków vs Warsaw for award availability: the honest answer is there's no meaningful difference, because the bottleneck is the AMS→SFO transatlantic leg and that's identical from both. Warsaw has slightly more AMS feeder frequency, which is a rounding error. Two upsides worth chasing: Flying Blue announces Promo Rewards on the 1st of each month at 25% off (18,750 economy), and Amex transfers 1:1 to Virgin Atlantic, which has NOT matched the AF/KLM surcharge hikes and can book the same KLM metal — that could cut the $875 meaningfully. Worth a look before you transfer.

LODGING, PULLED LIVE AT 5-PERSON OCCUPANCY. Kraków 7 nights Oct 26-Nov 2: Blue Angel 2BR $664 total ($95/night), Urban Nest Old Town 2BR $785 ($112/night), Mint Garden Kazimierz 2BR $854 ($122/night) — right in your verified $101-133 band. Kraków 6 nights: Blue Angel $607, Mint Garden $618 ($101-103/night). Kraków 2 nights carries a short-stay premium at $110-161/night. Warsaw 6 nights: Złota Heart of Warsaw 2BR $470 ($78/night) at the cheap end, solid central 2BRs $725-756 ($121-126/night) — Warsaw is slightly cheaper per night than Kraków but the savings are swamped by its worse airfare.

BOTTOM LINE: Kraków, arrive Oct 26, seven nights, fly out Nov 2 morning. $6,527 all-in cash for five, or about $4,040 plus 125,000 Amex MR. That is the cheapest Poland exit, the best version of the event, and the only shape where nobody sleeps in an airport.

leg: LANE 2 — DERRY / IRELAND (Dubrovnik Sun Oct 25 2026 → SFO, family of 5: 2 adults + 16/13/8)
summary:
FOUR THINGS CHANGED VS THE BRIEF, ALL VERIFIED LIVE TODAY (2026-08-03).

(1) THE DUBLIN FLIGHT IS NOT OCT-25-ONLY. I drove Ryanair's own booking engine at TRUE 5-passenger occupancy (4 adults + 1 child, the exact party). FR3881 DBV→DUB SELLS FIVE SEATS on Oct 25, Oct 27, Oct 28 AND Oct 30. Oct 26/29/31 the route does not operate at all. Oct 25 is the CHEAPEST, not the only. Also: the brief's "$705/5" was really EUR705/5 — at today's 1.1539 EUR/USD that is $814, and Basic Fare excludes checked bags. Realistic inbound with 3 bags + seat assignments (Ryanair forces a paid seat for the adult beside an 8yo): ~$1,033.

(2) THE DERRY LODGING CRISIS IS REAL, BUT IT IS EXACTLY ONE NIGHT. Live Booking.com at 2 adults + 3 children: Derry Oct 28-30 = 24 PROPERTIES, cheap ($449-$810 for 2 nights). Derry Oct 30-Nov 1 = 1 PROPERTY, and it is 20.8 miles out. Derry Oct 31 ALONE = "no properties found" — literally zero in the city on Halloween night; nearest is Culmore Point 4.5mi at $820 for ONE night. So the fix is not "give up on Derry," it is a SPLIT BASE: sleep in Derry Oct 27/28/29 (cheap, in the walls, and those are exactly the three Awakening trail nights), then move 33 minutes to Letterkenny, Co. Donegal for Oct 30/31 where 21 properties are open at $367-$811 for both nights. Drive in for the parade.

(3) THE TRANSPORT TRAP IS CONFIRMED AND IT COSTS YOU A NIGHT AND A DAY. Aircoach 705X (timetable valid to 23/12/2026) leaves Derry Foyleside every 2 hours; Derry→Dublin T2 is 4h05. The last coach that beats the 7pm Oct 31 parade is 16:55 — you'd miss the parade. After the ~8:15pm fireworks your first coach is 22:55, arriving Dublin Airport 03:00. By car it is 230 km / 3h04 free-flow (budget 3h30-3h45; the A5 is single-carriageway). Either way: SEEING THE OCT 31 PARADE FORCES A DUBLIN-SIDE NIGHT ON NOV 1 AND A NOV 2 DEPARTURE. That is fine — Nov 1 Dublin hotels for 5 are $169-$233, Nov 2 carries the identical $2,749 fare and the identical EI61 nonstop, and your Aer Lingus award space is confirmed Nov 2.

(4) LIE-FLAT OUT OF IRELAND EXISTS IN CASH ONLY, AND IT COSTS ~$14,600 EXTRA. Aer Lingus BUSINESS award = zero inventory (already verified). But CASH business on EI61 DUB→SFO Nov 2 DOES sell five: $17,327 for the party, nonstop, 11h05, lie-flat — I pulled it live at 5-pax. Nov 1 has NO nonstop business at 5. The cheaper lie-flat is repositioning DUB→LHR ($370/5) onto Virgin Atlantic Upper Class LHR→SFO Nov 1 at $15,461/5 — but that is a Nov 1 departure, which means abandoning the parade. So for THIS itinerary the lie-flat answer is EI61 business Nov 2 at $17,327.

Derry City & Strabane District Council PUBLICLY REBUTTED THIS ON 22 JUNE 2026, with committee chair Cllr Sandra Duffy saying attendees 'will not have to pay to attend the Awakening the Walled City Trail, but will be asked to register for the event to assist with crowd management,' and calling the £1 report 'inaccurate.' The £62 Family Pass covers only 2 adults + 2 children, so the a-la-carte is marginally cheaper here. (The £21.83 'summer' rate ends 1 Sep 2026 — you will pay full price in late October.) GIANT'S CAUSEWAY — the age bands work the OTHER way: child is 5-17, so all three kids fit the Family ticket (2 adults + up to 3 children) at £40 = $54, including reserved parking, half-hourly guided tours and audio guides. Or walk to the stones FREE and park at Innisfree Farm for £15 = $20. EPIC, DUBLIN: adults €21 x2 + 16yo €14.50 + 13yo €14.50 + 8yo €10.50 = €81.50 = $94; book 30+ days ahead for 20% off (~$75). PÚCA FESTIVAL (Oct 29 - Nov 1, Trim & Athboy, Co. Meath) — READ THIS BEFORE COMMITTING: the Big Top headliners (Glen Hansard, The Coronas, Róisín O, Hothouse Flowers, Jerry Fish) are STRICTLY 16+ and the Samhain Circus is STRICTLY 18+. Your 8- and 13-year-old are excluded from every marquee event. What they CAN do: Lighting of the Samhain Fire (Oct 31, Fairgreen Athboy — FREE, non-ticketed), the Púca Procession in Trim (FREE), the Trim Castle projections (FREE), Sorcas na Samhna (the non-18+ circus), heritage tours of Tlachtga, the circus workshop, and 'Beyond the Veil – The Púca Trail' at €20 + booking fee, 11am/12pm/2pm/3pm sessions Oct 29-Nov 1, meeting at the Harvest Market Information Hut in Trim (€100 = $115 for five). HARD CONFLICT: the Samhain Fire is Oct 31 in Athboy and the Derry parade is Oct 31 at 7pm in Derry — 3 hours apart by car. You get one. Take Derry; it is the better spectacle and the reason for this lane. If you want Púca, do the Trail on Thu Oct 29 — but Trim is 46 min from Dublin and Derry is 3h from Dublin, so Púca really wants to be a Dublin-bookend day, not a Derry detour. CLIFFS OF MOHER: €8 off-peak / €12 peak per adult online, under-12s free with a parent, so 2 adults + 16 + 13 pay = €32-48 = $37-55 for the party. BUT it is 270 km / 3h24 EACH WAY from Dublin Airport — a 7-hour round trip that does not fit a Dublin+Derry week. Either cut it or restructure around a Galway base (Dublin→Galway 218km/2h33, Galway→Derry 274km/4h00), which costs you two of the three Awakening nights. My recommendation: cut the Cliffs.

WHAT IS LIVE-VERIFIED vs MODELLED — read this before spending anything.

LIVE-PULLED THIS SESSION (Google Flights, true 5-passenger occupancy, one-way, USD totals for the party): every inbound connector and every exit fare quoted above. The encoder self-test reproduces the byte-identical URL from your earlier verified lanes, so the query shape is identical. Raw JSON for all 16 pulls is committed at /Users/jarredwinn/.omnara/worktrees/miscellaneous/wasabi-discern/data/raw/lane3-awe/ with a README mapping files to markets.

LIVE-PULLED (Booking.com, party of 5 = 2 adults + ages 16/13/8): every lodging figure. I confirmed the cards read "N nights, 2 adults, 3 children" so these are stay totals for the whole family; I divided to per-night myself.

MODELLED, NOT QUOTED: food per day, car hire, and activity bundles. These are the estimate component of every total, which is why I labelled all totals "aggregator-estimate" rather than "quoted-live" — the air and lodging are real quotes, the totals contain my modelling. Activity sub-components that ARE from published tariffs: Jungfraujoch (Jungfrau Railways 2026 published CHF fares), Plitvice (official 2026 fee schedule), Nærøyfjord cruise (Lustrabaatane published NOK fares).

AWARD SPACE — ONE IS VERIFIED, THE REST ARE NOT. The Aer Lingus AerClub DUB→SFO economy award (81,250 Avios + $973 for five) is the only redemption here with CONFIRMED inventory, carried from your prior lane: 6+ seats on Nov 1 and Nov 2. Every Flying Blue figure in this report is a PRICE assumption at the published 25,000/pp saver level with ~$220/pp fees — I did not verify saver bucket availability for five on any specific date, and Flying Blue reprices the whole party up if the bucket cannot hold everyone, so book 2 and 3 as separate awards. Do not treat the Madeira 1.73 cpp as bankable until someone checks actual space.

I DID NOT INVENT ANY FARE OR AWARD. Where a market returned nothing at five seats, I have said so and marked it unavailable (Azores STN→PDL n=0; Inverness STN→INV n=0; Ortisei zero properties sleeping five). Where inventory is thin I have given the itinerary count so you can judge the risk yourself (Madeira inbound n=2, Dolomites inbound n=3, Bergen→Dublin n=2).

THREE THINGS THAT WILL COST YOU MONEY IF IGNORED:
1. Do not fly London→Bergen directly ($3,153-3,227, n=2-4). Go via Oslo ($296). This single routing choice is worth ~$2,900.
2. Do not fly Zagreb→SFO directly ($4,068). Route through London ($340 + $2,206). Worth $1,522.
3. Exit dates are not interchangeable. Bergen collapses from $2,417 to $5,146 between Nov 2 and Nov 3. Oslo doubles from $2,112 to $4,253 between Nov 1 and Nov 2. Zurich moves the OTHER way and is $509 cheaper on Nov 3 than Nov 1. Pick the destination, then let the fare pick the date.

ON THE AWE SCORES: they are my judgement, not data, and I have adjusted them for late-October reality rather than quoting peak-season reputation. Norway is 8.5 not 10 because you get ~8 hours of daylight, ~2 hours of sunshine per day and 26 rain days per month — the ceiling is extraordinary and the floor is a wet grey week. Switzerland is 9 because 3,454m of altitude makes the payoff weather-independent. The Dolomites drop from a peak-season 9 to 6.5 purely because the lifts, rifugi and the Tre Cime road are closing around your dates.

ONE MORE OPTION WORTH NAMING: nothing stops you combining. Plitvice is only three nights and $362 to reach from Dubrovnik, and Zagreb→London is $340. You could do Plitvice at peak colour Oct 26-28, then fly to London and still exit on the cheapest deep-inventory transatlantic market in Europe — which is exactly the winning option above. If you want more, Plitvice plus Scotland routes through the same London hub for an extra $121 of air.

options.label: 9. SWITZERLAND / JUNGFRAUJOCH — highest raw awe, and the one place you must NOT use points
options.detail: Highest guaranteed awe on the list, and 'guaranteed' is the operative word — at 3,454m the Jungfraujoch is in snow and ice regardless of valley weather, so unlike Norway you are not gambling. The cog railway tunnels up through the Eiger north face to the highest railway station in Europe, opening onto the Aletsch Glacier. Base in the Lauterbrunnen valley: a U-shaped trench with 72 waterfalls off vertical walls, including the Staubbach dropping ~300m in free air. For an 8-year-old this is the most legible 'wow' here — the scale explains itself instantly.

caveats:
WHAT IS VERIFIED VERSUS WHAT IS NOT — read this before spending anything.

LIVE-VERIFIED AT TRUE 5-PASSENGER PRICING (2026-08-03):
• Every outbound cash fare in this table was pulled from Google Flights at 4 adult-fare + 1 child-age-8, where the displayed number is the PARTY TOTAL, not a per-person figure multiplied by five. Itinerary counts (n=) are given so you can judge 5-seat depth yourself.
• Every lodging figure was pulled from Booking.com at 2 adults + 3 children (16/13/8) in a single unit. Those are STAY TOTALS; the per-night figures are my division.
• Ryanair DBV→DUB and DBV→KRK dates, times and fares came from Ryanair's own booking engine and API at the exact party composition.
• FX at time of pricing: EUR→USD 1.153872, GBP→USD 1.348341.
• Raw JSON committed at /Users/jarredwinn/.omnara/worktrees/miscellaneous/wasabi-discern/data/raw/lane1-allsaints-poland/, /data/raw/lane2-ireland/ and /data/raw/lane3-awe/.

EXACTLY ONE AWARD HAS VERIFIED SPACE. Aer Lingus AerClub DUB→SFO economy: 16,250 Avios/pp off-peak, 6+ seats confirmed on Nov 1 AND Nov 2, ~$194.63/pp fees. That is it. EVERY Flying Blue number in this table — Kraków, Warsaw, Norway, Switzerland, Madeira, the Dolomites — is a PRICE ASSUMPTION at the published 25,000/pp saver level with estimated fees. Nobody has confirmed a saver bucket holds five on any specific date; that requires a logged-in award search. Do not treat any Flying Blue cents-per-point in this table as bankable until someone looks.

THE FLYING BLUE FEE IS AN ESTIMATE, NOT A QUOTE. $175/pp economy ($875 for five) is built from published Europe→US data points plus the 2026 surcharge increase (~$60 economy, ~$100 business). A comparable real data point — CDG→SEA business — came in at $523/pp. Only flyingblue.com at checkout gives your actual euro figure, and it moves the Poland award totals dollar for dollar. The Norway/Switzerland/Madeira/Dolomites $1,100 (~$220/pp) is the same estimate scaled for longer routings.

TWO OF YOUR ORIGINAL ANCHORS ARE STALE. You supplied KRK $3,379 and WAW $3,028. Re-pulled: KRK Nov 1 is $3,509 and WAW Nov 1 is $3,550 — Warsaw is $522 higher than your figure, which materially changed the Kraków-vs-Warsaw comparison. Airfare moves. Re-pull before committing.

MODELLED, NOT QUOTED, IN EVERY OPTION: food per day, rental cars, and activity bundles. That is why most totals are labelled aggregator-estimate rather than quoted-live — the air and lodging are real quotes; the totals contain my modelling. Activity sub-components that ARE from published tariffs: Jungfraujoch (Jungfrau Railways 2026 CHF), Plitvice (official 2026 fees), Nærøyfjord cruise (Lustrabaatane NOK), Titanic Belfast, Giant's Causeway, EPIC. The Ireland 7-seater at $850 is built from live Kayak tier floors plus sourced Irish Super-CDW ranges — NOT a booked quote; get a real one from Enterprise or Hertz direct, and note most US-issued Visa and Amex cards are EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED from rental coverage in the Republic of Ireland.

I DID NOT INVENT ANY FARE OR AWARD. Where a market returned nothing at five seats I said so and excluded it: the Azores (STN→PDL n=0), Inverness (STN→INV n=0), Ortisei (zero properties sleeping five), Santorini (seasonal shutdown plus a $3,420/n=4 exit), Tuscany (FLR→SFO $4,265 on n=4), the Faroes (formally advised against — 9.5 awe, but Vágar is fog- and gale-bound in late October and you have a hard California deadline).

THREE ROUTING DECISIONS WORTH REAL MONEY:
1. Do not fly London→Bergen directly ($3,153-3,227, n=2-4). Go via Oslo ($296). Worth ~$2,900.
2. Do not fly Zagreb→SFO directly ($4,068). Route through London ($340 + $2,206). Worth $1,522.
3. Exit dates are not interchangeable and the cliffs run in different directions. Bergen goes $2,417 → $5,146 between Nov 2 and Nov 3. Oslo doubles $2,112 → $4,253 between Nov 1 and Nov 2. Zurich moves the OTHER way and is $509 cheaper on Nov 3. Pick the destination, then let the fare pick the date.

THE STRUCTURAL RISK ACROSS ELEVEN OF TWELVE OPTIONS: everything except Plitvice hangs off a single Ryanair departure from Dubrovnik, because Ryanair remains the only carrier selling five seats ex-DBV. Ryanair DBV→DUB Oct 25 has already moved ~15% against your snapshot. Book the inbound first. Fallbacks exist (DBV→DUB also sells five on Oct 27/28/30; a DBV→Stansted→Dublin self-connect works on two tickets) but none are pleasant with five people and checked bags.

TIME-ORDER FOR BOOKING: (1) the Ryanair inbound, (2) Derry Oct 28/29 lodging or Flåm if you go north — both are the scarce nights, (3) confirm AerClub space in the booking flow BEFORE transferring Amex MR, because transfers are irreversible, (4) check the Flying Blue Promo Rewards announcement on the 1st of the month (25% off = 18,750 economy, which would drop the Poland award to ~94,000 miles for five) and check Virgin Atlantic, which transfers 1:1 from Amex, has NOT matched the AF/KLM surcharge hikes, and can book the same KLM metal — either could cut the $875 meaningfully.

ON THE AWE SCORES: they are my judgement, not data, and adjusted for late-October reality rather than peak-season reputation. Norway is 8.5 not 10 because you get ~2 hours of sunshine a day and 26 rain days a month. Switzerland is 9 because 3,454m makes the payoff weather-independent. The Dolomites drop from a peak-season 9 to 6.5 purely because the infrastructure is closing across your dates.
